clue.text: Prompt to follow Ken's partner, missing one alfresco meal

parts.note: Barbie is the doll paired with Ken
I = one, the Roman numeral; it is dropped, leaving BARBE
a cue prompts an actor

explanation.surface: A toy-box scene: someone is prodded to trail after Barbie while leaving somebody out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prompt' opens the clue and looks like a verb or an adjective, but it is the noun CUE, placed after the doll by 'to follow'.
explanation.definitionFit: A barbecue is a meal cooked and eaten outdoors, which is what alfresco means.

clue.text: Fighter needing some adrenaline

indicators.note: only part of the next word is used

parts.note: the answer sits across the fifth to seventh letters of the word

explanation.surface: A boxer who needs a rush of adrenaline before a bout.
explanation.walkthrough: Muhammad Ali, the boxer, is the fighter; the surface fits him so well the hidden word is easy to miss.
explanation.definitionFit: Muhammad Ali was a heavyweight boxing champion, a fighter by trade.

clue.text: Starters from brasserie likely including nuts in pancake

definitions.note: BLINI is strictly plural (singular blin), but English commonly treats it as a single pancake

indicators.note: the starting letters of the words that follow

parts.note: B-rasserie L-ikely I-ncluding N-uts I-n

explanation.surface: A menu warning that the brasserie's starters probably contain nuts in the pancake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starters' sits happily in a restaurant surface, where it means first courses rather than first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Blini are small Russian buckwheat pancakes; the plural is often used for a single one in English.

clue.text: Channel 4 game show about unknown part of Ireland

indicators.note: the game show goes around the unknown

parts.note: Countdown is a long-running Channel 4 word-and-numbers quiz
Y is a mathematical unknown; it goes in after COUNT

explanation.surface: A TV quiz with a segment about a mysterious corner of Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: Countdown is a British daytime TV quiz on Channel 4, famous for its letters and numbers rounds. County Down is in Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: County Down is one of the six counties of Northern Ireland, so part of the island of Ireland.

clue.text: Cryptic clue I had for mathematician

indicators.note: cryptic means puzzling or obscure, so the word's letters are disguised by rearranging

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging
I had contracts to I'd, giving ID

explanation.surface: A solver confesses that a cryptic clue gave them a mathematician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cryptic' reads as describing the clue, but it is the instruction to disguise the word 'clue' itself; 'I had' contracts as it would in speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Euclid was the ancient Greek geometer whose Elements founded classical geometry.

clue.text: Ornate style with gold around by Ms Chanel

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
Coco Chanel, the French fashion designer

explanation.surface: A fashion note: an ornate look trimmed with gold, by Coco Chanel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' reads as 'designed by' in the fashion surface, but in the wordplay it just means next to.
explanation.definitionFit: Rococo is the elaborate, highly decorated 18th-century style in art and architecture.

clue.text: Right measure of current inclination

parts.note: R = right
the amp is the unit of electric current

explanation.surface: Choosing the correct amount of electric current, or of a tendency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' suggests a river or the present day; here it is electrical.
explanation.definitionFit: A ramp is a slope, and an inclination can mean a slope or incline.

clue.text: Someone witty and clever, one with an ace up their sleeve?

definitions.text: one with an ace up their sleeve?

parts.note: a card is an amusing, eccentric person
sharp = quick-witted

explanation.surface: Describing a smart, funny person who always has a trick in reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as playful: a card sharp literally hides aces up the sleeve to cheat.
explanation.definitionFit: A card sharp cheats at cards, the stereotype being an ace hidden up the sleeve.

clue.text: Working together with Picaroon — get moving!

indicators.note: the letters are set in motion and rearranged

parts.note: the setter's own name plus GET, 11 letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: The setter urging the solver to get going and collaborate.
explanation.walkthrough: Picaroon is the setter of this puzzle, so the name reads as a signature, not as letters to scramble.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to cooperate is literally to operate together, which the prefix co- spells out.

clue.text: I tell fibs, probing head of McGill University's background

indicators.note: probing means poking into, so the fib-telling sits inside the other letters
the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: supplies its first letter M
to tell fibs is to lie

explanation.surface: Someone admits lying while investigating the background of McGill University.
explanation.walkthrough: I LIE goes inside M (head of McGill) and U (University).
explanation.definitionFit: A milieu is the social setting or surroundings someone lives in, which is their background.

clue.text: Tory PM eats nothing in African country

indicators.note: the PM takes the nothing inside

parts.note: David Cameron, Conservative prime minister 2010-16
O = zero, nothing; it goes in after CAMERO

explanation.surface: A former British prime minister going hungry on a visit to Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: Tory is the informal name for the British Conservative party; David Cameron was its prime minister from 2010 to 2016.
explanation.definitionFit: Cameroon is a country in west-central Africa.

clue.text: Ginger Spice with battered car — it's very old

parts.note: Ginger Spice of the Spice Girls is Geri Halliwell

indicators.note: battered means knocked about, so these letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging
the word it, with the 's read as a link meaning is

explanation.surface: Ginger Spice has a battered old car, and it's ancient.
explanation.walkthrough: The Spice Girls were a 1990s British pop group; Ginger Spice was Geri Halliwell. 'battered' rearranges CAR + IT into ATRIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Geriatric literally concerns the care of the elderly, and is used loosely to mean aged or decrepit.

clue.text: Sheltered by rogue state, a gentle property seller

indicators.note: the answer is sheltered inside the words that follow

parts.note: the answer starts at the last letter of 'rogue' and ends partway through 'gentle'

explanation.surface: A mild-mannered house seller given refuge by a pariah nation.
explanation.walkthrough: An estate agent is the British term for a real-estate agent or realtor. The comma after 'state' hides the join.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate agent sells houses and other property.

clue.text: US tennis champion's cricket trophy

parts.note: Arthur Ashe, Wimbledon and US Open champion
the possessive supplies the S

explanation.surface: An American tennis star who somehow owns a cricket trophy.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ashes is the cricket series between England and Australia, played for a tiny urn. The possessive 's is read literally as the letter S.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ashes is the trophy contested by England and Australia at Test cricket.

clue.text: Barristers accepting lawsuit — they hold documents

indicators.note: the barristers take the lawsuit inside

parts.note: brief is slang for a barrister or lawyer
a case is a lawsuit; it goes in after BRIEF

explanation.surface: Lawyers taking on a case and keeping the paperwork.
explanation.walkthrough: A barrister is a British courtroom lawyer, informally called a brief. The whole surface is legal, so the definition blends in.
explanation.definitionFit: A description rather than a synonym: the briefcase is named for carrying a lawyer's brief, a bundle of documents.

clue.text: Attempt to keep objective and up-to-date

indicators.note: the attempt holds the objective inside

parts.note: a try is an attempt
an end is an objective; it goes in after TR

explanation.surface: Trying to stay both impartial and current.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Objective' tempts as an adjective (unbiased) beside 'up-to-date', but it is the noun END.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal synonym: something trendy follows the latest trend, so it is current.

clue.text: I err badly, fooling around for a lark?

indicators.note: the letters mess about and change places

parts.note: nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone confessing to a serious mistake made while messing about for fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For a lark' reads as the idiom 'just for fun'; the definition is 'a lark', a person who rises early, and the question mark flags that sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A lark is someone who gets up early, which is what an early bird is.

clue.text: Ships from abroad oddly carrying bananas

indicators.note: carrying means holding within, so one part goes inside the other
oddly picks the letters in odd positions: first, third, fifth

parts.note: its odd letters give ARA
bananas is slang for crazy, mad

explanation.surface: Ships coming from overseas are loaded with bananas.
explanation.walkthrough: The bananas look like cargo, but here they are slang for crazy; the ships' 'carrying' is what puts that word inside the odd letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An armada is a fleet of warships, most famously the Spanish one of 1588.

clue.text: Puzzled personnel in urban area

indicators.note: the personnel go inside the urban area

parts.note: a town is an urban area
HR = human resources, the personnel department; it goes in after T

explanation.surface: Staff baffled by life in the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Puzzled' is the definition in the sense of confused, as in 'the question threw me'.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrown, informally, means disconcerted or puzzled.

clue.text: Key Greek character in old Greek city

parts.note: the Delete key on a computer keyboard
phi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: An important Greek figure living in an ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key Greek character' reads as a leading figure in a story; 'Key' is a keyboard key and 'character' a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Delphi was the ancient Greek city famous for its oracle.

clue.text: Wasted, as cherries may be

definitions.meaning: cherries often have their stones taken out before cooking

explanation.surface: Someone intoxicated, compared with a bowl of cherries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wasted' looks like 'thrown away', but it is the slang for intoxicated.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoned means intoxicated, and stoned cherries have had their stones removed.

clue.text: Lusty woodland deity took a pew by youngster, gutted

parts.note: to take a pew is to sit down
Y(OUNGSTE)R, emptied of its middle

explanation.surface: A randy forest god sitting in church beside a heartbroken child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gutted' is British slang for bitterly disappointed, which the surface uses; the wordplay takes it literally.
explanation.definitionFit: A satyr is a lustful Greek woodland god, part man and part goat.

clue.text: Monarch cutting high costs for hosiery items

indicators.note: cutting means slicing into, so the monarch goes inside the other letters
high in the sense of intoxicated, so the letters reel into a new order

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging
a king is a monarch

explanation.surface: A king slashes high prices for hosiery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high' looks like a description of the costs, but in its sense of drunk it is the signal to jumble that word.
explanation.definitionFit: Stockings are close-fitting leg coverings, a standard kind of hosiery.

clue.text: White House perhaps has one good bathroom

parts.note: I = one, the Roman numeral
G = good
loo is British for toilet

explanation.surface: A remark that the US president's residence has one decent bathroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'White House' points at Washington; 'perhaps' marks it as a definition by example, a house that is white because it is made of snow.
explanation.definitionFit: An igloo is a dome-shaped house built of snow blocks, so literally a white house.

clue.text: Outsize M&S skirts for British supermodel

parts.note: the letters M and S
OS = outsize, the clothing size label; it goes between M and S

explanation.surface: Large skirts from Marks & Spencer for Kate Moss.
explanation.walkthrough: M&S is Marks & Spencer, a British high-street clothing chain, and OS is its outsize label. Kate Moss is the British supermodel.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by description: Kate Moss rose to fame in the 1990s as one of the best-known fashion faces from Croydon, London.

clue.text: Moore and Travolta getting wine bottle?

parts.note: Demi Moore, the actress
John Travolta, the actor

explanation.surface: Two Hollywood stars fetching a bottle of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Each surname stands for the star's first name. The question mark allows that a demijohn is a large jar for making or storing wine rather than one on a dinner table.
explanation.definitionFit: A demijohn is a big narrow-necked bottle, commonly used for home winemaking.

clue.text: Lovers excited you

indicators.note: stirred up, so the letters move

parts.note: six letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A romantic pair who are thrilled with you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You' is the person reading the clue: in crosswords 'you' can be the solver.
explanation.definitionFit: The person doing the puzzle, addressed as you, is the solver.

clue.text: Regular servings of eclair for Biblical priest

indicators.note: letters taken at regular intervals

parts.note: E-c-L-a-I-r, first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: A priest being given regular helpings of cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Servings' fits the pastry surface; here it means letters served up at intervals.
explanation.definitionFit: Eli is the priest in the Book of Samuel who raised the young Samuel.

clue.text: A notorious London barber's in conflict

parts.note: used as it stands
Sweeney Todd, the murderous barber of Fleet Street, with the S of his possessive

explanation.surface: A killer barber's shop being caught up in a war.
explanation.walkthrough: Sweeney Todd is the fictional London barber who murdered his customers. The possessive 's is read as the letter S, and 's also reads as 'is' in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: people at odds disagree, as if backing opposite sides of a bet.

clue.text: Depicts primarily odious rogue like Kim Jong Un?

indicators.note: rogue in the sense of uncontrolled or out of line, so the letters go astray into a new order

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, picking the first letter

parts.note: supplies its first letter O

explanation.surface: A cartoon depicts an odious rogue resembling the North Korean leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rogue' rearranges DEPICTS plus O (first letter of odious, signalled by 'primarily').
explanation.definitionFit: Kim Jong Un rules North Korea as an absolute dictator, the very model of a tyrannical ruler.
